name: Kirpitcheck
description: Kirpitcheck is an open Python package that runs seven benchmarks of a gate-based quantum processor with a single call, run_suite(backend). Each benchmark compares the device with a value fixed by a theorem — two bits of clock–system information, a geometric phase of one half the enclosed solid angle, a recovery gain of one — rather than with a fit or a classical simulation of the ideal output, so its reference is the same at every size and on every platform. The central tool is a membrane interferometer: an ancilla reads the phase of one parity-sector state after a closed loop of parity-preserving two-qubit writes, and a retrace reference in the same run separates the geometric phase, proportional to the enclosed area, from coherent control error, which is independent of it. Injecting a known coherent error calibrates that separation on the device. On IBM Heron processors the per-state phase is |θ|/Ω = 0.4945 ± 0.0030 against 1/2 across two processors and an injected error is recovered with gain 1.00 ± 0.04. The package selects qubits from the live calibration, verifies every circuit against exact statevector values before submission, runs each benchmark as one Estimator job with readout mitigation and dynamical decoupling, and needs about two minutes of processor time for the full suite.
